questions.question: 🦅 Sami receives an anxious patient who is trembling in the chair. He says: 'We need to be firm, tell him to calm down!' 🐆 Mina replies: 'What if we tried empathy first?' What is the first step in managing an anxious patient?
options: Actively listen and acknowledge their anxiety without judgment
Firmly tell them to calm down
Ignore their anxiety and start treatment
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Active listening and acknowledging anxiety create a climate of trust.' 🦅 Sami: 'Fine, I'll try listening first...'

questions.question: 🐆 Mina, seeing a patient avoiding eye contact, says: 'He has important non-verbal communication.' 🦅 Sami replies: 'It's not serious, I focus on the teeth!' Why is non-verbal communication important?
options: It represents more than 50% of communication and reveals the patient's emotional state
It is not important in dentistry
questions.explanation: 🦅 Sami explains: 'Non-verbal language is crucial for understanding the patient.' 🐆 Mina: 'Sami, you're starting to take an interest in communication!'

questions.question: 🦅 Sami, seeing a crying child, says: 'We need to let them cry, it passes.' 🐆 Mina replies: 'We need to reassure and explain.' What is the best approach with an anxious child?
options: Use age-appropriate language, reassure, and explain the procedures
Scold them to make them stop
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'The child needs to understand and feel safe.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will try to be more patient with children.'

questions.question: 🐆 Mina, preparing for anesthesia, says: 'I will explain each step to the patient.' 🦅 Sami replies: 'That's a waste of time!' Why is explaining procedures important?
options: It reduces anxiety and gives the patient a sense of control
It's a useless waste of time
It only serves to make oneself look good
questions.explanation: 🦅 Sami explains: 'Explaining procedures reduces anxiety and improves cooperation.' 🐆 Mina: 'Sami, you are really making progress!'

questions.question: 🦅 Sami, seeing a phobic patient, says: 'We need to treat them under sedation.' 🐆 Mina replies: 'What if we tried relaxation techniques first?' What is a relaxation technique?
options: A method to reduce anxiety through breathing, distraction, or hypnosis
A method to put the patient to sleep
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Relaxation techniques are effective non-pharmacological tools.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will learn some breathing techniques.'

questions.question: 🐆 Mina, seeing a patient with clammy hands, says: 'This is a sign of anxiety.' 🦅 Sami replies: 'They're just hot!' What are the physical signs of anxiety?
questions.explanation: 🦅 Sami explains: 'Physical signs are valuable indicators of anxiety.' 🐆 Mina: 'Sami, you're starting to observe your patients!'

questions.question: 🦅 Sami, talking to a patient, says: 'Don't worry, it won't hurt.' 🐆 Mina intervenes: 'You shouldn't lie!' What is the right approach regarding pain?
options: Tell the truth about possible sensations while reassuring
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'We must be honest about sensations while reassuring the patient.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will be more transparent.'

questions.question: 🐆 Mina, seeing an agitated patient, says: 'I will offer them music.' 🦅 Sami replies: 'Music is useless!' What are the benefits of music in dentistry?
options: It reduces anxiety and masks treatment noises
questions.explanation: 🦅 Sami explains: 'Music creates a calming environment for the patient.' 🐆 Mina: 'Sami, you're discovering the benefits of music!'

questions.question: 🦅 Sami, seeing a patient with a fear of needles, says: 'We should show them the needle so they get used to it.' 🐆 Mina replies: 'Absolutely not!' Why should we not show the needle?
options: It can increase anxiety in a phobic patient
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Showing the needle can trigger a phobic reaction.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will hide the needle in the future.'

questions.question: 🐆 Mina, discussing with a patient, says: 'I understand your fear.' 🦅 Sami replies: 'It's not professional to show emotions!' Why is empathy important?
options: It creates a trusting relationship and reduces anxiety
questions.explanation: 🦅 Sami explains: 'Empathy is an essential professional skill.' 🐆 Mina: 'Sami, you're evolving!'

questions.question: 🦅 Sami, seeing a patient with severe dental phobia, says: 'We need to treat them under GA.' 🐆 Mina replies: 'What if we tried desensitization sessions first?' What is desensitization?
options: A gradual exposure to anxiety-provoking stimuli to reduce fear
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Desensitization allows the patient to gradually overcome their phobia.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will offer progressive sessions.'

questions.question: 🐆 Mina, seeing a silent patient, says: 'They may be afraid to speak.' 🦅 Sami replies: 'They're just shy!' How to encourage a patient to express themselves?
options: Ask open-ended questions and show interest
questions.explanation: 🦅 Sami explains: 'Open-ended questions encourage the patient to express themselves.' 🐆 Mina: 'Sami, you're learning communication!'

questions.question: 🦅 Sami, discussing with a patient, says: 'You don't have to be afraid, it's ridiculous.' 🐆 Mina intervenes: 'That's not how you reassure!' How to validate a patient's emotions?
options: Acknowledge their fear as legitimate and understandable
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Validating the patient's emotions is the basis of empathy.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will change the way I speak.'

questions.question: 🐆 Mina, seeing a patient with clammy hands, says: 'I will offer them a break.' 🦅 Sami replies: 'We don't have time!' Why is offering a break beneficial?
options: It allows the patient to refocus and reduce their anxiety
questions.explanation: 🦅 Sami explains: 'A short break can significantly reduce anxiety.' 🐆 Mina: 'Sami, you're starting to understand patients!'

questions.question: 🦅 Sami, seeing a patient with a phobia, says: 'It's genetic, we can't do anything.' 🐆 Mina replies: 'Not at all, we can treat it!' How is dental phobia treated?
options: Through a gradual approach, relaxation techniques, and psychological support
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Dental phobia is treatable through a multidisciplinary approach.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will train in these techniques.'

questions.question: 🐆 Mina, discussing with a patient, says: 'I will show you the instrument before using it.' 🦅 Sami replies: 'That's a bad idea!' Why is showing instruments beneficial?
options: It allows the patient to familiarize themselves with the instrument and reduce fear of the unknown
questions.explanation: 🦅 Sami explains: 'Showing instruments demystifies the treatment and reduces anxiety.' 🐆 Mina: 'Sami, you're right!'

questions.question: 🦅 Sami, seeing a patient with panic fear, says: 'We need to calm them with medication.' 🐆 Mina replies: 'What if we tried deep breathing?' What is deep breathing?
options: A simple relaxation technique to reduce anxiety
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Deep breathing is a powerful tool against anxiety.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will learn this technique.'

questions.question: 🐆 Mina, seeing a patient with a phobia, says: 'We need to work on the environment.' 🦅 Sami replies: 'The environment doesn't matter!' Why is the practice environment important?
options: A calming environment reduces anxiety and improves the patient's experience
The patient doesn't pay attention to the environment
questions.explanation: 🦅 Sami explains: 'The office atmosphere influences the patient's emotional state.' 🐆 Mina: 'Sami, you've become sensitive to the environment!'

questions.question: 🦅 Sami, discussing with a patient, says: 'You need to stop stressing.' 🐆 Mina intervenes: 'We should rather give them tools to manage their stress.' What tools can we offer?
options: Breathing techniques, relaxation, distraction, positive visualization
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Stress management tools are varied and adaptable.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will train in these techniques.'

questions.question: 🐆 Mina, seeing a patient with apprehension, says: 'I will talk to them about something else during the treatment.' 🦅 Sami replies: 'We need to focus on the treatment!' Why is distraction useful?
options: Distraction diverts the patient's attention from anxiety related to the treatment
questions.explanation: 🦅 Sami explains: 'Distraction is a validated technique to reduce anxiety.' 🐆 Mina: 'Sami, you're discovering the benefits of distraction!'

questions.question: 🦅 Sami, seeing a patient with a fear of cavities, says: 'It's irrational!' 🐆 Mina replies: 'All phobias are irrational, but real for the patient.' How to approach a phobia?
options: With empathy, acknowledging the fear and offering gradual solutions
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'We must approach phobias with respect and empathy.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will change my approach.'

questions.question: 🐆 Mina, seeing an anxious patient, says: 'I will give them a stress ball.' 🦅 Sami replies: 'That's ridiculous!' What are the benefits of manipulation objects?
options: They allow the patient to channel anxiety and focus on something else
questions.explanation: 🦅 Sami explains: 'Manipulation objects are simple but effective tools.' 🐆 Mina: 'Sami, you are open-minded!'

questions.question: 🦅 Sami, discussing with a patient, says: 'You don't have to be nervous.' 🐆 Mina intervenes: 'What if we normalized their nervousness?' Why is it important to normalize anxiety?
options: It allows the patient to feel understood and less isolated in their fear
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Normalizing anxiety reduces the patient's feeling of shame.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will normalize emotions.'

questions.question: 🐆 Mina, seeing a patient with a fear of noise, says: 'I will use audio headphones.' 🦅 Sami replies: 'Noise doesn't bother!' Why is noise anxiety-inducing in dentistry?
options: The noise of instruments can be perceived as threatening by the patient
questions.explanation: 🦅 Sami explains: 'Sharp noises can trigger anxiety.' 🐆 Mina: 'Sami, you are sensitive to patients!'

questions.question: 🦅 Sami and 🐆 Mina discuss the future of patient relations. Sami says: 'Teleconsultation will replace human contact!' Mina replies: 'Human contact remains irreplaceable.' What is the future of patient relations in dentistry?
options: Technology is a complement, but human contact remains essential
Human contact is no longer important
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Technology is a tool, but the human relationship is at the heart of care.' 🦅 Sami: 'I agree, we keep our humanity!'
